items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview

ctx.x: -- 65 Second Avenue, the home of Jacques Butler, February 6th, Stanley Crouch interviewing, and we are going to resume Gene Bullard and how he descended Sidney Bechet.

Well, the case was Mike McKenzie, Gene Bullard, come up to de les Tribune, the same region, which was Paris. I think this was around 1924 or something like that. See, this is Gene Bullard who was telling me about this thing. Sidney Bechet and Mike McKenzie were making records. So some change there that Mike McKenzie says, excuse me, but I think that's the wrong chord there. Bechet says, don't worry about it now, Bechet don't make no better chords. But he said, "But, see, it's a C 7 and you made it C-diminished"…

they had horses. So, "here you are," boom, boom, they started shooting, shooting at everything, he's drunk and he's shooting. Shot a couple horses in the leg. There's a man, a piano player from Chicago with me, (inaudible), shot him in the leg, shot a couple people, one lady in the head. Oh, it was awful. Then, after he run out of bullets, went home and went to sleep.
